summary: Crash and/or data corruption upon attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks
description: The bug Attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks causes the player to be unable to respawn. The game crashes (Exception generating new chunk caused by java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and/or the world is corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), and you become unable to open it again. "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" is spammed to the debug log. To reproduce 1. Create a new world. 2. Execute /worldborder center 50000000 50000000. 3. Execute /kill. 4. You are unable to respawn. 5. Attempt to go to title screen. 6. The game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new world.
3. Execute the command `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`.
4. Execute the command `/kill`.
5. Observe that you are unable to respawn.
6. Attempt to go to the title screen.
7. Observe that the game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center set over 30 million blocks, players experience a critical issue where they are unable to respawn, leading to game crashes or world corruption. Specifically, the game generates an exception due to new chunk generation, resulting in a java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and in some cases, a java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException occurs, making the world inaccessible. The debug log repeatedly shows the message "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)." To reproduce this bug, players should create a new world, set the world border center to coordinates 50,000,000 by 50,000,000 using the command /worldborder center 50000000 50000000, and then execute the command /kill. Following this, they will find themselves unable to respawn. Attempting to navigate to the title screen results in a crash or the world becoming unopenable. This issue not only disrupts gameplay but also risks significant data loss, as the affected world may become irretrievable.
Expected Behavior: When a player creates a world with a world border center set to over 30 million blocks and subsequently attempts to respawn after executing the /kill command, the game should allow the player to respawn normally without crashing. The world should remain accessible, and no error messages should appear in the debug log. The player should be able to navigate to the title screen without encountering any issues or data corruption, ensuring a seamless gameplay experience.
